scores.notes: Watson by the pawnbroker's has a broad, round face, a heavy dark waxed handlebar moustache and a stocky build; Watson in Wilson's room has a narrow, deeply lined face with a smaller brown moustache. The face shape and build conflict.
Watson seated in the train and Watson in Wilson's room both have a lean, angular face, short brown hair and a brown moustache, and look middle-aged. No clear identity cue conflicts.

Holmes at the desk and Holmes on the bed are both gaunt and clean-shaven, with swept-back dark hair, a long nose and hollow cheeks. The desk version looks a little more lined, but nothing clearly conflicts.

The felt-hat Watson and the train Watson are both heavyset, with a broad, jowly face and a thick walrus/handlebar moustache. The hair is slightly darker in the felt-hat scene, but well within the same brown range.

The left image shows a small white two-storey house burning on flat ground with fire-engines on the lawn. The right image shows only a smoke column rising from behind distant trees seen from the platform, so the house and grounds cannot be compared.

The left image shows a large white multi-chimney house burning below a hill. The right image shows only a distant smoke column and fire behind trees from the station, so it shows too little of the house or grounds to judge.

The train Watson and the street Watson by the pawnbroker's balls both have short brown hair, a full dark-brown handlebar moustache, an oval-to-broad face and a solid middle-aged build. No conflicting cue.
Holmes in the train and Holmes at the pawnbroker's corner are both gaunt and clean-shaven, with dark swept hair, a sharp nose and lined cheeks. The faces are consistent.

Watson in Wilson's room is slim, with a narrow younger face, dark hair and a dark moustache. The train Watson is heavyset and older-looking, with a broad, jowly ruddy face and lighter mid-brown hair. The face shape, build and hair shade conflict.

The left image shows only a distant fire and smoke on the horizon behind trees, seen from the platform at dusk. The right image shows a large white Georgian house burning in a valley, so the house in the left image cannot be compared.
Watson on the bed with the pistol and Watson in Wilson's room both have an oval face, short brown hair and a full brown moustache, and a medium build. There is no clear conflict.
Holmes in Wilson's room and Holmes at the desk are both gaunt and deeply lined, with swept-back dark hair and a long hooked nose. The faces are consistent.

The felt-hat Watson has a round, full-cheeked face with a very bushy handlebar moustache and wavy brown hair. The bed Watson has a narrower, hollow-cheeked face and a smaller moustache. The face shape conflicts.
Holmes on the bed and Holmes at the door in Wilson's room are both gaunt, long-faced and clean-shaven, with black swept-back hair. There is no conflicting cue.

The felt-hat Holmes has thick, wavy black hair and a smoother, younger, fuller face. The desk Holmes has thin, receding swept-back hair and a deeply lined, older, gaunt face. The hairstyle and age conflict.

The desk Holmes looks clearly older, with a receding brown-dark hairline and deep facial lines. The Holmes at the door in Wilson's room has full jet-black hair and a smooth, younger face. The age and hair conflict.

The left image shows only a distant fire and smoke behind trees beyond the station. The right image shows a small white two-storey house with a fire-engine and roses, but the house cannot be seen in the left image.
Holmes at the desk and Holmes by the pawnbroker's balls are both gaunt and deeply lined, with swept-back black hair and a hooked nose. They match closely.
Watson in Wilson's room and Watson on the street both have an oval face, dark-brown hair, a dark handlebar moustache and a medium build. They are consistent.
The train Holmes has a receding, slicked-back hairline and a gaunt, older face. The felt-hat Holmes has thick, wavy black hair and a younger, fuller face. The hairstyle and age conflict.
Holmes at the pawnbroker's corner and Holmes at the desk are both gaunt, lined and clean-shaven, with dark hair and a sharp nose. There is no clear conflict.
Watson on the street and Watson on the bed with the pistol both have short brown hair, a full brown handlebar moustache, an oval face and a medium build. They are consistent.
Holmes at the pawnbroker's corner and Holmes on the bed are both gaunt and clean-shaven, with dark hair and lined, hollow cheeks. They are consistent.
The street Watson and the felt-hat Watson both have dark-brown hair, a thick dark handlebar moustache and a solid build. The felt-hat face is somewhat fleshier, but no identity cue clearly conflicts.

The felt-hat Holmes has thick, wavy black hair and a younger, fuller face. The street Holmes has a receding, slicked-back hairline and a deeply lined, older, gaunt face. The hairstyle and age conflict.

The left image shows a modest white two-storey cottage with one end chimney, set among rose bushes. The right image shows a large symmetrical white Georgian mansion with several chimneys on a hillside. The architecture conflicts.
Both images show a brick cellar with barrel-vaulted arches, a stone flagstone floor and stacks of wooden crates along the walls, lit by a lantern. They plausibly show the same vault.
The felt-hat Watson and the street Watson both have a broad, ruddy face, a big bushy handlebar moustache, brown hair and a stocky build. They are consistent.

The felt-hat Holmes looks around 60, with grey-streaked, heavily receding hair and a deeply wrinkled face. The Holmes at the door in Wilson's room has full jet-black hair and a smooth, younger face. The age and hair colour conflict.

Holmes in bedroom (left) vs examining hat (right): both clean-shaven with dark slicked-back hair, receding temples, long gaunt face and hooked nose; right looks slightly more lined but same individual.
Holmes on bed vs Holmes in railway carriage: same dark swept-back receding hair, narrow gaunt clean-shaven face and aquiline nose.

Left burning house is a large symmetrical two-storey white house with hipped slate roof, three chimneys and pedimented porch; right is a smaller gabled cottage with a chimney on the gable end. The architecture conflicts.

Left Holmes (hat scene) has thick, full, wavy dark hair and a younger, fuller face; right Holmes on the bed has receding, swept-back hair and a gaunt, older, hollow-cheeked face. Hair and age conflict.
Both show a brick barrel-vaulted cellar with arched side passages, stacked wooden crates and cracked flagstone floor, lit by a lantern. Compatible layout from different viewpoints.
Holmes at desk vs in carriage: both have dark hair swept back from a high receding hairline, long gaunt clean-shaven face and prominent hooked nose.
Watson on bed (left) is lean with a narrow angular face; Watson in carriage (right) is heavy-set with jowly, ruddy fuller face and broader build. Face shape and build conflict.

Watson behind Holmes in Wilson's room has a narrow, gaunt face, dark hair and swarthy complexion; Watson in armchair (right) has a broader, rounder face, lighter brown side-parted hair and a large upturned walrus moustache. Face shape conflicts.
Holmes in carriage vs Holmes by the door: same receding black hair swept back to the collar, long gaunt clean-shaven face and aquiline nose.
Holmes at door (left) and outside pawnbroker's (right, in hat): both dark-haired, clean-shaven, lean long face with strong nose and similar age; hat hides hair on right but nothing conflicts.
Holmes at pawnbroker's (hat on) vs examining the felt hat: both gaunt, clean-shaven, dark-haired with long hooked nose; right looks somewhat more lined but no clear identity conflict.

Watson in Wilson's room has a lean narrow face with dark hair and clean chin; Watson on the bed has a broad heavy face with grey-flecked stubble and greying sideburns, looking older. Age and grizzled-stubble cue conflict.
Watson in carriage has a long narrow lean face and brown hair; Watson on the bed has a broad, heavy face with grey stubble and greying sideburns. Face shape and age conflict.
Holmes at pawnbroker's corner vs in carriage: same dark receding swept-back hair, long gaunt clean-shaven face and hooked nose.
Holmes in carriage vs at his desk: same slicked dark receding hair, gaunt clean-shaven long face and aquiline nose.
Holmes at pawnbroker's vs by the door in Wilson's room: same gaunt face, receding swept-back dark hair, clean-shaven, hooked nose.
Holmes by the door vs on the bed: both gaunt, clean-shaven with receding dark hair swept back and long nose; bed figure is small but consistent.
Holmes in carriage vs on the bed: same dark swept-back receding hair, gaunt clean-shaven face and aquiline profile.
Holmes at desk vs examining hat: both gaunt, clean-shaven, dark slicked receding hair, long hooked nose, deep cheek lines.

Watson in carriage has a long, narrow, lean face and modest moustache; Watson in armchair (hat scene) has a broader, rounder face with full cheeks and a large curled walrus moustache. Face shape conflicts.
Watson on the bed is lean with a narrow face; Watson in the hat scene is heavy-set, jowly and broad-faced with a scowl. Build and face shape conflict.
Holmes on bed vs at desk: same receding dark hair swept back, gaunt clean-shaven long face and aquiline nose.
Watson at pawnbroker's has a broad, ruddy face with dark hair and full dark moustache; Watson in carriage has a long narrow lean face. Face shape conflicts.
Watson in hat scene is heavy and jowly with a broad scowling face; Watson in Wilson's room has a longer, leaner face. Face shape and build conflict.
Holmes on bed vs at pawnbroker's: same gaunt clean-shaven face, dark receding swept-back hair and hooked nose.
Holmes examining hat vs in carriage: both gaunt, clean-shaven, dark slicked receding hair, long aquiline nose.
Holmes by door vs in carriage: same dark swept-back hair, long lean clean-shaven face and strong nose.

Watson on the bed has grey-flecked stubble, greying sideburns and grizzled moustache, looking older; Watson at pawnbroker's has a dark moustache, dark hair and clean chin. Grey stubble vs clean dark-haired is the conflicting cue (pawnbroker figure is small).
Holmes by the door has receding swept-back hair and a gaunt older face; Holmes in the hat scene has thick full wavy dark hair and a younger, fuller face. Hairline and age conflict.
